correctness.rationale: For a connected graph, the two-step Laplacian condition forces uniform firing count. In a primitive two-cycle it is exactly one per vertex; the chip-threshold intervals then supply the cut weight without overcounting. On trees, independent cut bits yield the functional-map expansion and unique-star lower extremum. The nonnegative rooted DP and exact Pell addition identities establish an upper bound strictly improved when any rooted branching is merged, giving unique path maximization. Direct state-space checks, rooted DP checks, and exact addition identities were replayed from packaged standard-library scripts. These checks are finite corroboration; the all-order mathematical proof is in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The natural question left open by known tree periodicity is the size, rather than mere existence, of the oscillatory state population. This gives exact sharp extrema across all labelled n-vertex trees, uniqueness, an exponential structural gap from star to path, and a constructive combinatorial/DP reason for the bounds; it is not a numerically fitted finite table.
